description: Java is a high-level, class-based, object-oriented programming language designed to have as few implementation dependencies as possible.

topics.title: Java Basics
topics.content:
Java Basics

Java is an object-oriented programming language produced by Sun Microsystems (now Oracle). It is platform-independent, meaning "Write Once, Run Anywhere" (WORA).

Hello World Example

public class Main {
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        System.out.println("Hello, World!");
    }
}

Every Java program must have at least one class and a main method which is the entry point of the application.

topics.title: Data Types
topics.content:
Data Types in Java

Java is a strongly typed language. Every variable must have a declared type.

Primitive Data Types

  • int: 32-bit integer.
  • double: 64-bit floating-point.
  • boolean: true or false.
  • char: 16-bit Unicode character.
int age = 25;
double price = 19.99;
boolean isValid = true;
char grade = 'A';

topics.title: Control Statements
topics.content:
Control Statements

Control flow statements break up the flow of execution by employing decision making, looping, and branching.

If-Else and Loops

int x = 10;
if (x > 5) {
    System.out.println("x is greater than 5");
} else {
    System.out.println("x is 5 or less");
}

// For Loop
for (int i = 0; i < 5; i++) {
    System.out.println(i);
}

topics.title: OOP Concepts
topics.content:
Object-Oriented Programming (OOP)

Java's core paradigm is OOP. The four main pillars are:

  • Encapsulation: Hiding internal state (using private) and requiring all interaction to be performed through an object's methods.
  • Inheritance: Creating new classes based on existing ones using the extends keyword.
  • Polymorphism: The ability of an object to take on many forms (method overriding and overloading).
  • Abstraction: Hiding complex implementation details and showing only the essential features.
public class Animal {
    public void makeSound() {
        System.out.println("Some sound");
    }
}

public class Dog extends Animal {
    @Override
    public void makeSound() {
        System.out.println("Bark");
    }
}

topics.title: Interfaces
topics.content:
Interfaces

An interface is a completely "abstract class" that is used to group related methods with empty bodies.

public interface Drawable {
    void draw();
}

public class Circle implements Drawable {
    public void draw() {
        System.out.println("Drawing a circle");
    }
}

Since Java 8, interfaces can also contain default and static methods with implementations.

topics.title: Collections Framework
topics.content:
Java Collections Framework

The Collections framework provides an architecture to store and manipulate a group of objects.

Common Interfaces and Classes

  • List: ArrayList, LinkedList (Ordered, allows duplicates).
  • Set: HashSet, TreeSet (Unordered, no duplicates).
  • Map: HashMap, TreeMap (Key-Value pairs).
List<String> names = new ArrayList<>();
names.add("Alice");
names.add("Bob");

Map<String, Integer> ages = new HashMap<>();
ages.put("Alice", 28);

topics.title: Exception Handling
topics.content:
Exception Handling

Exceptions are used to handle errors gracefully without crashing the program.

try {
    int result = 10 / 0;
} catch (ArithmeticException e) {
    System.out.println("Cannot divide by zero!");
} finally {
    System.out.println("This block always executes.");
}

Java categorizes exceptions into Checked (compile-time) and Unchecked (runtime) exceptions.

topics.title: File Handling
topics.content:
File Handling (I/O)

Java provides the java.io and java.nio packages for reading and writing data to files.

import java.nio.file.*;

// Writing to a file
Path path = Paths.get("example.txt");
Files.writeString(path, "Hello File!");

// Reading from a file
String content = Files.readString(path);
System.out.println(content);

topics.title: Generics
topics.content:
Generics

Generics enable types (classes and interfaces) to be parameters when defining classes, interfaces, and methods. They provide stronger type checks at compile time.

public class Box<T> {
    private T item;
    public void set(T item) { this.item = item; }
    public T get() { return this.item; }
}

Box<String> stringBox = new Box<>();
stringBox.set("Hello");

topics.title: Stream API
topics.content:
Stream API

Introduced in Java 8, the Stream API is used to process collections of objects in a functional and declarative manner.

List<String> names = Arrays.asList("John", "Jane", "Jack", "Doe");

// Filter and print names starting with 'J'
names.stream()
     .filter(name -> name.startsWith("J"))
     .forEach(System.out::println);
